origin_year_or_period.value: developed from the Croad Langshan in the 1890s

conservation_status.value: rare, declined in popularity through the 1930s and has only just survived

value: lighter, more game-like build than the Croad Langshan, sometimes compared to the Modern Game
only lightly feathered legs, unlike the more heavily feathered Croad Langshan
not a good producer of eggs or meat
the split between Modern Langshan and Croad Langshan breeders led to separate clubs, with the Croad Langshan Club forming in 1904

history_summary.value: The Modern Langshan was bred from the Croad Langshan, imported to Britain from northern China in 1872, by selecting for a taller, tighter-feathered bird to distinguish it from the Black Cochin. It was popular for a time but declined through the twentieth century and is now rarely seen.
